summary: Convert a raster data cube into a vector data cube
description:
Converts a raster data cube into a vector data cube by grouping connected pixels with exactly the same value into polygons (also known as "polygonize").

The polygons follow the pixel boundaries and may contain holes. Pixels are connected if they share an edge or, if `connectivity` is set to `8`, also if they share a corner. Areas with the same value that are not connected result in separate polygons. No polygons are created for no-data values.

As pixels are only grouped if their values are exactly equal, this process is meant for categorical data, e.g. land cover classes or masks. Continuous data should be quantized first, e.g. with ``linear_scale_range()`` and ``round()``.

The data cube must only contain the spatial dimensions `x` and `y`, as the polygons may differ for each label of other dimensions (e.g. for each date or band). Otherwise, a `TooManyDimensions` exception is thrown. Use processes such as ``filter_bands()``, ``reduce_dimension()`` or ``drop_dimension()`` to remove other dimensions beforehand.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: A raster data cube with only the spatial dimensions `x` and `y`.

parameters.name: connectivity
parameters.description: Defines which pixels are connected: `4` connects pixels that share an edge, `8` also connects pixels that share a corner.

returns.description: A vector data cube with a single dimension of type `geometry`. The geometries are polygons in the spatial reference system of `data`, the values are the pixel values of the corresponding areas. The order of the geometries is not defined.

TooManyDimensions.message: The data cube must only contain the spatial dimensions `x` and `y`.
